download_breed_picture.description: Download a dog picture as a file, so a later step can attach it to an email, upload it to a chat or put it in storage. Name a breed for a picture of it, pass a picture's id from an earlier step for that exact picture, or give neither for a random breed. The credit its licence requires comes back with the file. No API key required.

get_breed.description: Get one breed in full: what it weighs and how tall it stands in both kilograms and pounds, how long it lives, where it came from, what its coat is like, how it behaves on ten rated scales, the clubs that recognise it, and any pictures with the credit each one's licence requires. Name it however you have it, a name or an id. No API key required.

get_breed_picture.description: Get a picture of a breed, or of a random breed, at whichever size the message needs, with the credit its licence requires already written out in text and in HTML. The pictures come from Wikimedia Commons under their authors' licences, which means the credit has to be shown wherever the picture is, so it comes back with it. Most breeds have no picture yet, and a breed without one says so rather than failing silently. No API key required.

get_facts.description: Get one to five random dog facts, each a sentence ready to put straight into a message. The service picks different ones every time and marks the answer uncacheable, so a step that runs daily says something new each day. No API key required.

mock_response.fact: Many foot disorders in dogs are caused by long toenails.

facts.body: Many foot disorders in dogs are caused by long toenails.

parameters.description: Optional. How many facts to return. Between 1 and 5; 1 by default. The service caps it at five itself, and says nothing about having done so, so anything higher comes back as five.

requested_count.description: How many were asked for after the service's own cap of five was applied.

get_group.description: Get one breed group and every breed in it, by name or by id. "Herding" finds the Herding Group: the word the API appends is optional. Each breed comes back as an id and a name, which is what Get a breed takes for the rest of it. No API key required.

parameters.description: The breed group, by name or by the id from an earlier step. The word "Group" is optional, so "Herding" finds the Herding Group. List breed groups shows them all.

returns.description: One breed group and the breeds in it.

breed_count.description: How many breeds belong to the group.

breeds.description: The breeds in the group, by id and name.

items.description: A breed as a pointer: the API names a group's breeds by id alone, so this is the id, the name filled in here, and nothing else. Pass the id to Get a breed for the rest.

has_images.description: True when there is a picture of it to show.

list_breeds.description: Browse the API's 340-odd breeds, a page at a time, narrowed to the ones worth looking at: one breed group, one country, one coat, one kennel club, the hypoallergenic ones, the sizes you want, or only the breeds that have a picture. Order them by name, by weight or by how long they live. No API key required.

match_breeds.description: Find the breeds that suit what a household can actually offer. Say what matters (good with children, quiet, little shedding, an hour of walking at most, an apartment, hypoallergenic) and get the breeds that clear every bar, ranked by how comfortably they clear it, each saying why it is on the list. The ratings are the richest thing the API holds and it has no way to search them, so this is the recommendation they are for. Breeds nobody has rated yet are counted and reported rather than dropped quietly. No API key required.

description: Pull researched dog breed data into a workflow from the Dog API: over 340 breeds, each with its weight and height in both metric and imperial, how long it lives, where it came from, its coat, its temperament and ten behaviour ratings from energy to how well it does with children. Find a breed from anything a person typed, browse the catalogue by group, country, coat, size or kennel club, and ask which breeds actually fit an apartment, a household with children or an hour of walking a day. Pictures come back with the credit their licence requires, ready to embed or download, and there is a random dog fact for the steps that just need something to say. No account or API key required.
